To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a bacterial extract from the isolate Serratia spp. ARP5.0 showed a promising potential to control postharvest body rot and root and crown rot of avocado.

a bacterial extract from a Serratia sp., isolated from a rhizospheric sample of avocado plants, showed biocontrol capacity against the avocado pathogens Colletotrichun gloeosporiodes and Phytophthora cinamomi.

a bacterial extract and its emulsion formulates showed promising results for controlling fruit body rot and seedling root rot in avocado, and that these products could be developed into new bioproducts for the avocado industry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new biotechnological strategies for avocado production.
the development of new products for the control of fruit and root diseases in the Hass avocado.
the development of new biotechnological tools to improve the quality of the avocado fruit, and to increase the sustainability of the avocado industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work demonstrated that bacterial extracts can be used for the control of fungal diseases on avocado fruits and seedlings.
the bacterial extract obtained from Serratia sp ARP5.1 showed bioactivity against the pathogens tested and could be a good candidate as an alternative to chemical fungicides in avocado crops.
the bacterial extract and emulsion formulations showed promising results for controlling avocado pathogens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bacterial extracts are promising for the control of fruit body and root rot in avocados.

the bacterial extract and emulsion formulate were able to reduce body rot in avocado fruits and root rot in seedlings.

the extract from Serratia sp., ARP5.1 is a promising bioproduct for the control of fruit body and root rots in avocado.
